capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction and both biconditionals. The key observation is that every constituent proposition is a canonical universal-property/coherence fact, so the implications may prove their conclusions independently of their hypotheses.

- First establish the standard limit-cone identity
  \[
  (\operatorname{conePointUniqueUpToIso}(P,Q))^{-1}\,;\,s.\pi_j=t.\pi_j.
  \]
  This is the defining compatibility of the unique isomorphism between two limiting cones.

- For the product/opposite-coproduct equality, use morphism extensionality for the product cone. After taking `unop`, compare the two maps after every product projection. The defining equations of `opProductIsoCoproduct'` reduce those component equations to the preceding limit-cone identity. Thus the comparison isomorphisms are independent of the chosen limiting cone.

- Obtain finite products in \(C\) by dualizing finite coproducts in \(C^{\mathrm{op}}\): opposite the chosen finite coproduct cocones and their universal properties.

- Finally, characterize `biproductIsoPi.inv` by its composites with the biproduct projections. Each such composite is the coordinate projection \(\operatorname{LinearMap.proj}_j\), exactly the stated ModuleCat morphism.

The common mechanism is uniqueness from universal properties: limits, colimits, and biproducts force all the displayed comparison maps and projection formulas.
